rationale: Both documents share the exact same title ('The text/enriched MIME Content-type') and cover the identical specific topic: defining the 'text/enriched' MIME type within the framework of RFC 2046 (MIME). The OLDER document (RFC1563, 1994) explicitly references a previous 'text/richtext' definition. The NEWER document (RFC1896, 1996) presents the same definition without that specific historical reference, functioning as an update to the standard for this specific content type. In the context of RFCs, when a later document shares the exact title and scope of an earlier one in the same series, it is treated as a replacement (superseding) rather than an amendment or unrelated companion. The date difference (1994 vs 1996) confirms the newer version is the current reference.

label: unrelated
rationale: Both documents address the CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) protocol, but they serve different specific purposes within that ecosystem. RFC8230 (2017) is a specialized document defining how to use RSA algorithms specifically for COSE messages. RFC9052 (2022) defines the fundamental structures and processes of the COSE protocol itself (signatures, MACs, encryption, key representation). In IETF standards practice, a document defining core structures (RFC9052) is not considered to supersede a document defining a specific algorithm usage within that framework (RFC8230); rather, they coexist. RFC9052 does not restate or revise the RSA-specific content of RFC8230; it provides the foundational framework upon which RFC8230's specific algorithm definitions would apply. Therefore, they are companion documents covering related but distinct scopes within the same family.
